name: Plain-English Marker Translations
purpose: Provide short, plain-English impact and meaning text for curated marker IDs without changing evidence strength or claim boundaries.
do_not_claim: A translation makes a marker easier to read; it does not increase evidence, establish a diagnosis, measure a current phenotype, or replace the marker's claim boundaries.
If a marker is missing or uncalled, the translation is not evidence of presence or absence.

fallback.simpleMeaning: A dedicated plain-English explanation is not yet available for this marker. Treat the technical interpretation as a probabilistic association, keep the marker's claim boundaries in view, and use symptoms, measured labs, and clinical context before acting.

translations.simpleMeaning: This is a research-only marker for DNA repair. It requires a doctor's confirmation and more clinical testing before making any health decisions.
This is a research-only marker for DNA repair. It requires a doctor's confirmation and more clinical testing before making any health decisions.
This gene change is considered harmless and does not indicate a classic hereditary cancer risk. It is a common variant used in research.

translations.simpleImpact: APOE e4-associated marker (lipid and brain-health context)
translations.simpleMeaning: This marker is part of the APOE type used in lipid and age-related health research. Associations with cholesterol and other outcomes vary by the complete APOE type, ancestry, age, and health history; a lipid profile and clinical context are more useful than this SNP alone.
This is one of the markers used with rs429358 to infer a common APOE type. This SNP alone does not establish the full type or your current cholesterol; use a lipid profile and clinical context.

This region marker has been associated with coronary-disease outcomes in some studies. The effect is probabilistic and overlaps with blood pressure, lipids, smoking, diabetes, family history, and other factors; it is not an early-heart-attack prediction.
This NOS3 marker has been studied in nitric-oxide signaling and vascular response. Associations vary between studies; it does not measure nitric oxide, blood flow, or exercise recovery.

This NOS3 marker has been studied in relation to nitric-oxide signaling and vascular response. It is a small-effect research association, not a measurement of vessel relaxation or cardiovascular disease.

translations.simpleImpact: COL1A1 bone and collagen association marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This COL1A1 marker has been associated with small differences in bone or connective-tissue traits. Effects are probabilistic and do not establish bone weakness or injury risk; symptoms, fracture history, and clinical testing matter more.
This COL5A1 marker has been studied in tendon, ligament, and flexibility traits. Associations vary; it does not predict an injury or establish whether a person is unusually flexible.
This common marker is not a diagnosis of a collagen disorder. It has been studied in relation to small differences in joint and tissue flexibility, but symptoms and clinical examination matter more.

This GDF5 marker has been studied in cartilage and osteoarthritis susceptibility. Any association is small and probabilistic; it does not diagnose osteoarthritis or predict which joint becomes symptomatic.
This MMP3 marker has been studied in tissue-remodeling traits in joints and tendons. Associations vary and may be small; it does not determine tendon integrity or predict an Achilles injury.

This common marker has been studied in connective-tissue and vascular traits. It does not establish vessel fragility, aortic disease, or a condition such as Marfan syndrome; clinical examination and family history are more informative.
This common variant is linked to natural variations in height and bone length. It is not harmful and represents normal human diversity.

Two copies are associated with absence of an ACTN3 protein in fast fibers in relevant research. Training, health, and many other genes influence performance, so this does not determine an endurance or sprint profile.
This COL12A1 marker has been studied in ligament and injury-related traits. Some studies report associations with ligament injury, but effects vary and it does not predict an ACL tear.
This MMP9 marker has been studied in tissue-remodeling and vascular or joint traits. Associations vary; it does not measure tissue function or establish joint or heart disease.

This AOC1 marker has been studied in DAO-related histamine processing. Food tolerance varies widely, and this SNP does not diagnose histamine intolerance, food allergy, hives, or a need to avoid particular foods.

This HNMT marker has been studied in cellular histamine processing. Symptoms and food responses are not determined by this SNP; consider allergies, medicines, other conditions, and clinical evaluation when symptoms persist.
Two copies are associated with adult lactase non-persistence in many European-ancestry studies. Symptoms and dairy tolerance vary, and this is not a milk-allergy diagnosis.

translations.simpleImpact: FTO appetite and weight association marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This FTO marker has been associated with small differences in appetite or weight-related traits in some populations. It does not determine appetite or body size; eating patterns, activity, sleep, environment, and health history matter.
This PPARG marker is studied in fat storage and insulin sensitivity. Associations are modest and context-dependent; it does not establish insulin sensitivity or protection from type 2 diabetes.

translations.simpleImpact: KCNQ1 glucose and insulin-secretion association marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This KCNQ1 marker has been associated with small differences in insulin secretion or glucose-related traits. It does not diagnose diabetes or predict an individual response; HbA1c, glucose testing, and clinical risk factors are more useful.

This is a well-studied common association with type 2 diabetes risk, but it is not a diagnosis or a personal probability estimate. Glucose, HbA1c, family history, age, body composition, activity, sleep, and overall diet provide the actionable context.

This SLC30A8 marker is studied in zinc transport and pancreatic beta-cell function. Any association with glucose or diabetes risk is probabilistic; it does not measure insulin release or diagnose diabetes.

This KCNJ11 marker has been studied in pancreatic beta-cell function and glucose traits. It does not measure post-meal insulin or establish diabetes risk for one person; use laboratory testing and clinical context.

translations.simpleImpact: GCKR glucose and triglyceride association marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This GCKR marker has been associated with a trade-off between fasting glucose and triglyceride-related traits in some studies. A lipid panel and glucose testing show current status; the SNP is not a diagnosis.
This APOA5 marker has been associated with triglyceride levels in some populations. Diet, alcohol, metabolic health, medicines, and other genes also matter; a measured lipid panel is needed.

This variant has been associated with differences in an enzyme involved in blood-fat clearance. Some studies link it with lower triglycerides or higher HDL, but your actual lipid tests and overall health matter more.
This marker has been associated with differences in cholesterol transport and HDL levels. It does not guarantee protection; a complete lipid profile and ApoB-related context are more useful.

This LPA marker has been associated with higher lipoprotein(a) in many studies, but the SNP does not measure your level. A measured Lp(a) result, lipid profile, family history, and overall cardiovascular risk are needed for useful interpretation.

This LPA marker is associated with a smaller lipoprotein(a) form and may be associated with higher Lp(a) in some people. A measured Lp(a) test is needed; the SNP alone is not a cardiovascular diagnosis.

This MC4R-region marker has been associated with small differences in appetite or weight-related traits. It does not determine hunger or eating behavior; food environment, sleep, activity, and health history matter.
This FKBP5 marker has been studied in stress-response regulation. Associations vary by stress exposure and other factors; it does not measure cortisol or determine emotional responses.

This research-level HTR2A marker has been studied in serotonin-related traits and medication-response research. It does not measure receptor density, diagnose a mood condition, or predict a medication response.

This OXTR marker has been studied in oxytocin-related and social-behavior research. Findings are inconsistent and context-dependent; it does not determine bonding, empathy, personality, or how someone handles stress.

translations.simpleImpact: Slower breakdown of brain chemicals (MAOA gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This MAOA marker has been studied in neurotransmitter metabolism and behavior research. It does not measure brain-chemical levels or determine emotional responses, aggression, or personality.

translations.simpleImpact: Slower dopamine breakdown in the brain (COMT gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one COMT allele component studied in dopamine and catechol-estrogen breakdown. Effects are small and context-dependent; it does not determine focus, anxiety, personality, or hormone levels.
This DRD2/ANKK1-region marker has been studied in dopamine signaling and reward-related traits. It does not measure receptor number or determine motivation, addiction, or reward-seeking behavior.

This DRD2 marker has been studied in dopamine signaling and cognitive traits. Associations are small and inconsistent; it does not measure receptor availability or determine memory, learning, or flexibility.

This research-level CNTNAP2 marker has been studied in brain connectivity, language development, and sensory traits. It does not establish a neurodevelopmental condition or predict an individual's abilities.
This minor research marker has been studied in brain structure, sensory processing, and neurodevelopmental traits. The association is weak and does not predict an individual's traits or diagnosis.
This ADRA2A marker has been studied in norepinephrine signaling and attention-related research. It does not measure receptor sensitivity or predict focus, stress response, or medication outcome.
This ESR1 marker has been studied in estrogen-receptor and hormone-response research. It does not measure current estrogen, determine hormone sensitivity, or explain menstrual mood symptoms.
This research-level ESR1 marker has been studied in estrogen-receptor and symptom-timing research. It does not measure estrogen or explain emotional or physical symptoms during a hormone change.
This PGR marker has been studied in progesterone-receptor and menstrual-symptom research. It does not measure progesterone, determine receptor sensitivity, or diagnose a cycle-related mood condition.
This BDNF marker has been studied in neuroplasticity, memory, and exercise-response research. Associations vary; it does not measure BDNF, predict learning ability, or establish exercise response.
This FAAH marker has been studied in endocannabinoid signaling and stress-related traits. It does not measure anandamide, diagnose anxiety, or predict stress resilience.

This ADORA2A marker has been associated with differences in caffeine sensitivity in some studies. Dose, sleep, expectations, medicines, pregnancy, and personal response matter; it does not diagnose anxiety or set a universal caffeine limit.

translations.simpleImpact: OPRM1 pain and reward association marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This OPRM1 marker has been studied in endorphin signaling, pain, and reward-related traits. Associations are small or inconsistent; it does not determine pain tolerance, social bonding, or medication response.
This DBH marker has been studied in dopamine-to-norepinephrine metabolism. It does not measure neurotransmitter levels or determine focus, stress response, or medication outcome.

This common variant may modestly affect folate-related lab values in some people, especially with two copies, but it does not mean you cannot process folic acid. Do not avoid folic acid or replace it with a supplement solely because of this genotype; use diet, labs, pregnancy context, and clinician guidance.

This common variant is usually a small-effect context marker. It does not diagnose a folate problem or justify avoiding folic acid; consider folate, B12, and homocysteine only when clinically relevant.
This IL6 marker has been studied in inflammatory signaling and measured IL-6 differences. It does not measure current inflammation or predict how someone feels during illness or stress.

This TNF marker has been studied in inflammatory signaling. Associations vary by population and context; it does not measure current TNF levels, diagnose inflammation, or establish autoimmune disease.

This HFE variant can be relevant to iron-overload evaluation, especially when a clinical result and iron studies support it. A raw SNP result alone does not diagnose hemochromatosis or prove that you absorb too much iron.
This is a milder HFE component. Its significance depends on other HFE alleles, iron studies, symptoms, and life stage; it is not proof of iron buildup by itself.

translations.simpleImpact: Altered folate and B12 processing (MTR gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This MTR marker is studied in folate and vitamin-B12 pathways. Any effect is likely small and context-dependent; it does not establish a vitamin deficiency or determine supplement need.
This MTRR marker is studied in vitamin-B12 recycling. It does not measure B12 status or set a personal dietary requirement; symptoms, diet, absorption, medicines, and laboratory results matter.

translations.simpleImpact: Reduced Vitamin B12 delivery to cells (TCN2 gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This variant has been studied in vitamin-B12 transport. If symptoms or labs raise concern, clinicians may consider more than a single serum B12 result; the SNP alone does not establish cellular B12 deficiency.

translations.simpleImpact: FUT2 secretor-status and B12 association marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This FUT2 marker has been associated with secretor-status and B12 differences in some populations. One SNP does not establish secretor status or B12 deficiency; symptoms, diet, and labs provide the useful context.

This PEMT marker is studied in choline metabolism. It may be a reason to consider ordinary choline-rich foods in the context of your diet and health, but it does not establish a choline deficiency or fatty-liver risk.
This MTHFD1 marker is studied in folate and choline pathways. Any effect is likely context-dependent; it does not set a personal daily choline requirement or justify high-dose supplements.

translations.simpleImpact: Slightly less active Vitamin D receptors (VDR gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This VDR marker is associated in some studies with small differences in vitamin-D signaling. Use 25(OH)D and clinical context rather than the SNP to decide whether any action is needed.
This VDR marker has been studied in vitamin-D signaling. It does not measure receptor number or current vitamin-D status; use a 25(OH)D result and clinical context rather than the SNP alone.

translations.simpleImpact: Lower Vitamin D transport in the blood (GC gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This GC marker has been associated with differences in vitamin-D transport or measured levels in some populations. A blood test, not the SNP alone, shows your current vitamin-D status.

translations.simpleImpact: Less efficient Vitamin D activation in the liver (CYP2R1 gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This CYP2R1 marker is studied in vitamin-D activation. Effects vary; use measured 25(OH)D and clinician guidance rather than assuming supplementation is needed.
This DHCR7 marker is associated in some studies with vitamin-D-related differences. It does not measure sunlight exposure or establish reliance on supplements; use labs and safe sun/food guidance.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2D6*4 no-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one no-function CYP2D6 allele component. A clinical CYP2D6 diplotype and copy-number result are needed before discussing a medicine; do not change medication from this SNP alone.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2C9*3 reduced-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one reduced-function CYP2C9 allele component. A clinical diplotype, the specific drug, and prescribing context are needed before estimating medication effects.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2C9*2 reduced-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one reduced-function CYP2C9 allele component. It is not a complete medication-response result; use validated clinical PGx interpretation and a clinician or pharmacist.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2C19*17 increased-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one CYP2C19 increased-function allele component. A full diplotype and the specific medication are needed; do not assume ultra-rapid metabolism from this SNP alone.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2C19*2 loss-of-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele component. A clinical diplotype and drug-specific guideline are needed before discussing clopidogrel or another medication; this SNP alone is not a phenotype.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2C19*3 loss-of-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele component. It should be combined with the other allele and the drug-specific guideline in a validated clinical PGx result.

translations.simpleImpact: SLCO1B1 reduced-function allele component — statin context needs clinical review
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one SLCO1B1 transporter allele component studied in statin response. The statin, full haplotype, symptoms, and clinical guidance matter; do not start or change a statin from this SNP alone.

This CYP1A2 marker is one contributor to caffeine-response research. Your response also depends on dose, sleep, smoking, medicines, pregnancy, and other factors; use your symptoms and blood pressure rather than a DNA-only limit.

translations.simpleImpact: VKORC1 warfarin-sensitivity allele component — clinical dosing required
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one VKORC1 component used with CYP2C9, CYP4F2, clinical factors, and INR monitoring when warfarin is prescribed. It does not determine a dose by itself.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP4F2 warfarin-dose component — clinical dosing required
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one CYP4F2 component considered in warfarin dosing. The complete clinical PGx result, diet, other medicines, and INR monitoring matter; it does not set a dose by itself.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP3A5*3 splice allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is a CYP3A5 splice-variant component. A clinical genotype, ancestry-aware interpretation, and the specific medication are needed; it is not a broad result for all medicines.

translations.simpleImpact: CYP2B6*6 reduced-function allele component — clinical PGx needed
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one CYP2B6 reduced-function allele component. The complete diplotype, medication, and clinical guideline are needed before discussing exposure or dose.

translations.simpleImpact: Reduced transport of uric acid and statins (ABCG2 gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This ABCG2 marker is studied in uric-acid handling and transport of some medicines. It may modify gout or medication context, but it is not a gout diagnosis or a medication-dose result.

translations.simpleImpact: DPYD*2A toxicity-risk allele component — urgent clinical confirmation if relevant
translations.simpleMeaning: If this allele is confirmed by a clinical DPYD test, it can be important before fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy. A raw consumer call is not enough to choose, avoid, or dose treatment; oncology and PGx guidance are required.

translations.simpleImpact: Rare DPYD toxicity-risk allele component — urgent clinical confirmation if relevant
translations.simpleMeaning: If this rare allele is confirmed clinically, it may affect fluoropyrimidine safety. Do not infer treatment from a raw array call; an oncology team must use validated DPYD testing and current guidance.

translations.simpleImpact: DPYD reduced-function allele component — clinical confirmation if relevant
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one DPYD allele component studied for fluoropyrimidine toxicity. Confirm it clinically and let the oncology team interpret the complete result before treatment decisions.

translations.simpleImpact: TPMT reduced-function allele component — thiopurine safety requires clinical testing
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one TPMT allele component. A clinical TPMT/NUDT15 result, blood-count monitoring, and the prescribing guideline are needed before interpreting thiopurine risk.

translations.simpleImpact: TPMT*3C allele component — thiopurine safety requires clinical testing
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one TPMT allele component and can contribute to a TPMT diplotype. Confirm clinically with TPMT/NUDT15 guidance; do not infer a dose or stop treatment from this SNP alone.

translations.simpleImpact: NUDT15 reduced-function allele component — thiopurine safety requires clinical testing
translations.simpleMeaning: This is one NUDT15 allele component studied for thiopurine toxicity. Confirm with a clinical PGx result and blood-count monitoring before any treatment decision.
This ADA marker has been studied in adenosine metabolism and sleep-pressure traits. It does not predict sleep depth or morning alertness; sleep schedule, health, medicines, and environment matter.
This research-level PER2 marker has been studied in circadian timing and sleep traits. It does not diagnose insomnia or predict awakenings; sleep history and clinical context matter.

This CLOCK marker has been associated with chronotype in some studies. It does not determine whether someone is a night owl or measure melatonin; light exposure, schedule, sleep pressure, and environment also matter.

translations.simpleImpact: Altered sugar control in the morning (MTNR1B gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This MTNR1B marker has been associated with fasting-glucose and glucose-timing traits. It does not measure melatonin or insulin release; sleep timing, meals, medicines, and glucose testing provide the useful context.

This DIO2 marker has been studied in thyroid-hormone conversion. It does not measure tissue thyroid activity or explain fatigue/brain fog; thyroid symptoms and laboratory results require clinical interpretation.

This GPX1 marker has been studied in antioxidant-enzyme activity and thyroid-related research. It does not measure selenium status or establish a need for selenium; food, laboratory results, medicines, and clinician guidance matter.

This CTLA4 marker has been associated with autoimmune traits in some studies. It does not measure immune activity or diagnose an autoimmune condition; symptoms, examination, and appropriate tests are needed.

translations.simpleImpact: Altered immune signaling and autoimmune risk (PTPN22 gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This PTPN22 marker has been associated with several autoimmune traits. Associations vary by condition and population; it does not diagnose autoimmune thyroid disease or predict an individual outcome.
This CD40 marker has been studied in antibody and autoimmune-trait research. It does not measure thyroid antibodies or diagnose thyroid disease; symptoms and laboratory testing are required.

This TSHR marker has been studied in thyroid signaling and autoimmune-thyroid traits. Associations vary by condition and population; it does not measure receptor sensitivity or diagnose thyroid disease.

translations.simpleImpact: Altered thyroid hormone conversion in organs (DIO1 gene)
translations.simpleMeaning: This DIO1 marker has been studied in thyroid-hormone conversion and measured hormone-ratio differences. It does not measure current thyroid function or determine treatment; laboratory results and clinical assessment matter.

This ESR1 marker has been studied in estrogen-receptor and reproductive-trait research. Associations vary by study and population; it does not measure current estrogen, establish hormone sensitivity, or explain cycle-linked mood symptoms.

This ESR2 marker has been studied in estrogen-receptor and reproductive-trait research. It does not measure current estrogen, determine receptor sensitivity, or diagnose a menstrual or reproductive condition.

This ESR2 marker is a research association in hormone-response studies. Effects vary by study, ancestry, and context; it does not measure estrogen or predict cycle symptoms, fertility, or treatment response.

This PGR marker has been studied in progesterone-receptor and reproductive research. It does not measure progesterone, show whether a progestin or progesterone will be tolerated, or diagnose a cycle-related condition.

This PGR marker has been studied in hormone-response research. Associations are context-dependent; it does not measure progesterone, identify a contraceptive ingredient, or predict an individual medication response.
This CYP19A1 marker is studied in steroid and estrogen-production research. It does not measure current estrogen, establish aromatase activity, or justify hormone or supplement changes.

This CYP19A1 marker has been studied in aromatase and steroid-biology research. Any association is probabilistic; it does not measure current hormone levels or predict menstrual symptoms or treatment response.
This CYP17A1 promoter marker is studied in steroid-biosynthesis research. It does not measure current androgen or estrogen levels, diagnose an endocrine condition, or determine hormone treatment.

This SHBG marker has been associated with differences in sex-hormone binding or measured levels in some studies. A blood test is needed for current SHBG and hormone status; the SNP does not diagnose an imbalance.
This SHBG promoter marker is studied in sex-hormone-binding research. It does not measure current free or total hormone levels, explain cycle symptoms, or establish a need for treatment.
This FSHR marker has been studied in ovarian and reproductive response. It does not measure FSH, ovulation, ovarian reserve, fertility, or the response to fertility treatment.
This FSHR marker is studied in follicle-stimulating-hormone signaling. Associations vary; it does not measure current hormone levels, ovarian reserve, fertility, or treatment response.
This LHCGR marker has been studied in luteinizing-hormone and reproductive signaling. It does not measure LH, ovulation, pregnancy, fertility, or response to reproductive medication.
This SRD5A2 marker is studied in conversion of testosterone-related hormones. It does not measure current testosterone or DHT, diagnose an androgen condition, or determine hormone therapy.

This SRD5A2 marker has been studied in androgen metabolism. Effects are probabilistic and body- and context-dependent; it does not measure hormone levels or predict hair, prostate, sexual, or reproductive outcomes.

This CYP1A1 marker is studied in estrogen and chemical-metabolism pathways. It does not measure estrogen clearance, detoxification, cancer risk, or medication safety; use clinical history and testing when relevant.
This CYP1B1 marker has been studied in catechol-estrogen metabolism. It does not measure current estrogen or establish cancer risk, detox capacity, or a need to avoid a food or medicine.
This CYP1B1 marker is studied in estrogen and xenobiotic metabolism. Associations vary; it does not measure current hormone levels, diagnose disease, or predict medication response.
This CYP1A1 marker has been studied in estrogen and chemical-metabolism pathways. It does not measure enzyme activity, current estrogen, detoxification, or medication safety.

This UGT1A1 marker is studied in bilirubin and glucuronidation pathways, including research involving steroid compounds. It does not measure current estrogen clearance or determine drug safety; bilirubin and medication decisions need clinical context.
This UGT1A1 allele component is studied in bilirubin and drug-metabolism research. It does not establish a UGT1A1 phenotype, measure estrogen, or determine medication choice or dose by itself.
This SULT1A1 marker is studied in sulfation and hormone-metabolism research. It does not measure estrogen levels or metabolic capacity, and it is not a reason for a detox plan or medication change.

This SHBG marker has been studied in hormone-binding differences. It does not measure free testosterone, estradiol, or current hormone exposure; use measured labs and clinical context when appropriate.

This RGS7 locus has been reported in research related to premenstrual symptoms. It is not a validated PMDD test and does not explain an individual's irritability, avoidance, or treatment response; prospective symptom timing and clinical review matter.
This marker is included as a research placeholder for cellular responses to ovarian-steroid change. Evidence is limited and it does not diagnose PMDD, measure hormones, or predict symptoms.

This WNT4 locus has been studied in endometriosis susceptibility research. It is a small, probabilistic research association; it does not diagnose or exclude endometriosis, adenomyosis, pelvic pain, or fertility problems.
This locus has been studied in endometriosis susceptibility research. It does not diagnose or exclude endometriosis or adenomyosis, and it cannot explain an individual's symptoms or fertility.
This GREB1 locus is a research association reported for endometriosis-related traits. It does not diagnose or rule out endometriosis, adenomyosis, pelvic pain, or a hormone disorder.

This intergenic locus has been studied in endometriosis susceptibility research. The association is probabilistic and does not diagnose or exclude endometriosis, adenomyosis, or a person's cause of pain.
This ID4 locus has been studied in endometriosis susceptibility research. It does not diagnose or exclude endometriosis or adenomyosis, and it does not predict an individual clinical outcome.
This locus has been studied in endometriosis susceptibility research. It is not a diagnostic test and does not establish the cause of pelvic pain, bleeding, or fertility difficulty.
This VEZT locus is a research association reported for endometriosis-related traits. It does not diagnose or exclude endometriosis, adenomyosis, or any individual's pelvic symptoms.

This COMT marker is studied as part of a haplotype in catecholamine and estrogen-response research. It does not measure COMT activity, estrogen, neurotransmitters, or explain cycle-linked mood symptoms by itself.
This COMT marker is interpreted with other variants in some catecholamine and hormone-response research. It does not measure estrogen, dopamine, mood, or medication response on its own.

This marker can be one part of the CYP2D6*10 allele. It may affect how some medicines are processed, but a complete CYP2D6 diplotype and clinical drug guidance are required; this SNP alone does not select or dose a medicine.
This marker can contribute to a decreased-function CYP2D6 star allele. It must be interpreted with the other chromosome, additional variants, and copy-number status before any medication decision.

This marker can contribute to CYP2D6*17, which is more common in some African-ancestry populations. Use a complete, clinically interpreted CYP2D6 diplotype; the marker alone does not predict an individual medicine response.
This marker can be part of a no-function CYP2C19 allele. A full CYP2C19 diplotype and the specific medicine are needed; do not start, stop, or change a medicine from this SNP alone.
This marker can contribute to reduced CYP2C9 activity for some medicines. Interpret it with a complete CYP2C9 diplotype and drug-specific clinical guidance, not as a standalone dosing instruction.
This marker can contribute to CYP2C9*8, an allele that may be missed by limited ancestry-focused panels. A complete clinical diplotype and the medicine being considered are required before acting.

This marker contributes to SLCO1B1 transporter haplotypes that can affect exposure to some medicines. Interpret it with rs4149056 or a validated haplotype result and drug-specific guidance; it is not a statin-safety verdict by itself.

This proxy marker has been studied in relation to simvastatin-associated muscle risk. Direct SLCO1B1 haplotype testing, the exact statin, symptoms, and clinician review are more informative than this proxy alone.

This marker can be part of a DPYD haplotype associated with fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk. Because the decision is high-stakes, confirm the complete DPYD result clinically before treatment; this SNP is not a diagnosis or treatment order.

This marker can reduce TPMT activity and may matter when thiopurines are considered. Clinical TPMT/NUDT15 interpretation and, when appropriate, enzyme testing are required; it does not set a dose by itself.
This rare NUDT15 marker may contribute to thiopurine intolerance risk. Rare consumer-data calls need clinical confirmation and full NUDT15/TPMT guidance before treatment decisions.

This is one component of G6PD deficiency interpretation. Enzyme activity, ancestry-relevant variants, the exact medicine, and clinical review may be needed; this marker alone cannot clear or prohibit an exposure.

BCHE variation can contribute to prolonged response to certain anesthetic medicines. A complete clinical history and, when indicated, enzyme or dibucaine testing are more useful than this marker alone; tell the anesthesia team about any confirmed result.

This marker contributes to NAT2 haplotypes that may affect metabolism of isoniazid and other compounds. A full haplotype and medicine-specific clinical guidance are required; it does not predict toxicity by itself.

This marker can be part of CYP3A4*22 and may alter exposure to some CYP3A medicines. Drug interactions, organ function, and the exact medicine often matter more; use clinical PGx guidance rather than changing treatment from this SNP.

This marker can contribute to the CYP2C8*3 haplotype, which has been studied for some NSAIDs and oncology medicines. Confirm the haplotype and use medicine-specific guidance; it is not a general NSAID or cancer-treatment instruction.

This marker has been studied in nicotine metabolism and smoking-cessation research. The phenotype may require additional variants or copy-number information, and it does not determine smoking behavior or a treatment choice.

This CES1 marker has been associated with dabigatran exposure in some studies. Kidney function, age, dose, interactions, and current clinical guidance are essential; the SNP alone is not a bleeding-risk calculation.

This rare CES1 marker may affect metabolism of methylphenidate or other ester prodrugs. Confirm a rare call clinically and combine it with medication response and prescriber guidance; it does not establish a dose or diagnosis.

This marker was important in older interferon-based hepatitis C treatment research. Modern direct-acting antivirals have changed its relevance, so current hepatology guidance matters more than this SNP alone.

This marker represents a clinically important BRCA1 founder variant in the curated resource. A consumer-DNA call is not a diagnosis; confirm it with clinical testing and genetic counseling before medical decisions.

This marker represents a clinically important BRCA1 founder variant in the curated resource. Consumer-array indel calls can be unreliable, so clinical confirmation and genetic counseling are required before interpretation.

This marker represents a clinically important BRCA2 founder variant in the curated resource. Confirm any consumer-DNA call with a clinical laboratory and genetic counselor; it is not a final cancer diagnosis.

This rare BRCA1 marker is treated as confirmation-required in the curated resource. A raw-DNA call may be false positive or represented differently; clinical testing and genetic counseling must come first.

This CHEK2 marker is associated with a moderate-penetrance cancer-susceptibility context in the curated resource. Confirm the variant clinically and interpret it with family history and variant-specific counseling.

This CHEK2 marker is a lower-penetrance susceptibility association, not equivalent to every pathogenic CHEK2 variant. Clinical confirmation, family history, and a risk model are more useful than this SNP alone.

This APC marker has been associated with moderate colorectal-cancer risk in some ancestry groups. It is distinct from classic familial-adenomatous-polyposis variants and should not replace clinician-guided screening.

This MUTYH marker is a clinically relevant variant that requires confirmation. The key interpretation depends on whether another pathogenic MUTYH variant is present, so one consumer-DNA call cannot diagnose a recessive syndrome.
This MUTYH marker is a clinically relevant variant that requires confirmation. Distinguishing carrier status from two pathogenic variants needs a complete clinical test and genetic counseling.

translations.simpleImpact: MITF melanoma and kidney-cancer susceptibility context
translations.simpleMeaning: This MITF marker is a moderate or low-penetrance susceptibility association in some research. Family history, skin findings, pigmentation, UV exposure, and clinical assessment matter more than this SNP alone.

This HOXB13 marker is associated with prostate-cancer susceptibility in some ancestry groups. It is not diagnostic and does not replace a clinician-guided screening discussion using family history and current health context.

This CHRNA5 marker has been associated with nicotine dependence or smoking intensity in some studies. It is exposure-behavior context, not a high-penetrance lung-cancer diagnosis or a reason to infer someone's behavior.
This common 8q24 marker is a small-effect research association reported for colorectal and prostate cancer traits. It belongs in a calibrated polygenic model, not stand-alone clinical risk reporting.

This common FGFR2-region marker is a small-effect breast-cancer research association. It is not clinically actionable by itself and should not change screening outside an appropriately calibrated risk assessment.
This common TOX3-region marker is a small-effect breast-cancer research association. It is useful only as part of validated risk modeling, not as a stand-alone prediction or diagnosis.
This common MAP3K1 marker is a small-effect breast-cancer research association. Do not overinterpret it or use it alone to alter screening or treatment decisions.

This common MSMB marker is a small-effect prostate-cancer research association. It belongs in a calibrated polygenic model and does not replace PSA, family-history, or clinician-guided screening decisions.

This repeat marker can contribute to UGT1A1*28 and may matter for irinotecan toxicity in a drug- and dose-specific context. Consumer SNP data may not represent repeat length reliably; use clinical PGx guidance.

This HRH1 marker was associated with adenomyosis in a recent large research study, but it is not a diagnostic test. Results may vary by ancestry and phenotype definition; clinical history and indicated imaging matter more than this SNP, and an uncalled result is unknown.

This indel is one component of a CYP2D6 star allele associated with absent enzyme activity. A consumer call needs clinical confirmation and the complete diplotype, including copy-number review, before any medication discussion.

This deletion can contribute to a no-function CYP2D6 star allele. It is not a complete metabolizer result; indel detection, both star alleles, copy number, and the exact medication require clinical PGx review.
This rare CYP2C19 marker is used as one component of a clinical star-allele call. A raw-DNA result needs confirmation and the other allele before discussing drug metabolism or treatment options.
This marker can be part of a no-function CYP2C19 star allele. It does not assign a metabolizer phenotype by itself; use a confirmed diplotype and medication-specific clinical guidance.
This marker can contribute to a no-function CYP2C19 allele. Rare raw-array calls need clinical confirmation and complete diplotype interpretation before they are used in medication decisions.
This marker is one part of a CYP2C19 star-allele interpretation. It cannot establish a poor-metabolizer phenotype or guide a dose without clinical confirmation, the second allele, and the exact drug.

This marker can contribute to a reduced-function CYP2C9 diplotype. Drug effects are medication-specific and depend on the other allele and clinical factors; confirm with a clinical PGx test before acting.
This CYP2C9 marker is one component of a decreased-function allele. It does not provide a warfarin, NSAID, or other drug dose; a confirmed diplotype and prescribing guidance are required.

This marker can contribute to an SLCO1B1 reduced-function haplotype involved in hepatic drug transport. Statin or other medication context requires the complete clinical haplotype, drug, dose, interactions, and symptoms.

This marker is part of DPYD HapB3 research and clinical-PGx context. It is not a chemotherapy dosing result; confirm the haplotype with a clinical laboratory before fluoropyrimidine treatment decisions.

This rare marker may contribute to reduced NUDT15 activity and thiopurine-toxicity susceptibility. It requires clinical confirmation and complete TPMT/NUDT15 interpretation; it must not be used alone to choose a dose.

This marker can contribute to a G6PD A or A- haplotype. One SNP cannot diagnose G6PD deficiency or establish medication safety; enzyme testing and a clinically interpreted genotype are more appropriate when relevant.
This NAT2 marker can contribute to a slow-acetylator haplotype. It does not establish a phenotype or an isoniazid plan by itself; full haplotype and medication monitoring context are needed.
This marker is one component used to infer NAT2 acetylator status. The full haplotype, drug, liver health, and monitoring plan matter more than this single consumer-DNA call.
This marker can contribute to NAT2 slow-acetylator context. It cannot assign a personal drug response or dose without the full clinical haplotype and medication-specific review.
This marker is one component of the CYP2C8*3 haplotype. Any medication implication is drug-specific and requires a confirmed haplotype, complete clinical context, and prescriber review.
This CYP2C8 marker has been studied in metabolism of selected medicines. Effects are context-dependent and do not provide a dose or treatment recommendation from raw DNA alone.

This indel has been used in interferon-era hepatitis C response research. Consumer data may not represent it reliably, and current antiviral decisions depend on the infection, treatment options, and clinical assessment.

This CYP2E1 marker has been studied in alcohol, solvent, and anesthetic metabolism. The enzyme is strongly affected by exposures and metabolic state, so this SNP does not predict alcohol safety or anesthesia response.

This MC1R marker is associated with red-hair or fair-skin biology in some people and can add melanoma-susceptibility context. It is not a melanoma diagnosis; visible phenotype, UV exposure, skin examination, and family history matter more.

This MC1R marker is associated with pigmentation and UV-sensitivity traits in some populations. It does not establish melanoma or make UV exposure safe; use skin phenotype, exposure history, and clinical examination.

This MC1R marker is part of pigmentation and melanoma-susceptibility research. Any effect is probabilistic and not diagnostic; dermatology assessment, skin findings, UV exposure, and family history remain important.

This LRP5 marker has been associated with small differences in bone mineral density in some studies. It does not diagnose osteoporosis or predict a fracture; age, fracture history, loading, hormones, medications, and DXA are more informative.

This LRP5 marker is part of bone mineral-density research. Any association is small and probabilistic; it does not measure your bone density or replace clinical risk assessment and DXA when indicated.

This WNT16 marker has been studied in cortical bone density and fracture-related traits. It does not establish fragile bones or fracture risk for one person; bone history, mineral status, activity, and clinical testing matter more.

This WNT16 marker contributes to research on bone density. It is not an osteoporosis test and does not determine whether resistance or weight-bearing activity is safe; symptoms, history, and clinical assessment lead.
This SOST marker has been studied in Wnt signaling and bone mineral-density traits. Effects are probabilistic and do not diagnose osteoporosis or determine a bone treatment or supplement dose.

This TNFRSF11B marker is part of research on bone resorption and remodeling. It does not measure bone turnover or establish fracture risk; clinical history, mineral labs, and DXA are more useful when indicated.
This RANKL/TNFSF11-region marker has been studied in bone density and remodeling. It is a small-effect association, not a diagnosis or a reason to start, stop, or change osteoporosis treatment.

This CASR marker is part of calcium-sensing and mineral-balance research. It does not diagnose a calcium or parathyroid disorder; measured calcium, PTH, kidney context, symptoms, and clinician review are more informative.
This SP7 marker has been studied in bone formation and mineral-density traits. Effects are probabilistic and do not diagnose osteoporosis, predict a fracture, or determine a supplement or treatment.

This CPED1/WNT16 marker has been studied in bone mineral density and fracture-related traits. It does not measure bone density or establish osteoporosis; fracture history, mineral status, and clinical assessment matter more.

This CASR marker is part of calcium-sensing and mineral-balance research. It does not diagnose a calcium or parathyroid disorder; measured calcium, PTH, kidney context, symptoms, and clinician review are more informative.

translations.simpleImpact: ESR1 bone and estrogen-response context marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This ESR1 marker has been studied in estrogen signaling and bone-density traits. It does not measure current estrogen, menopause status, or hormone response, and it does not prescribe hormone therapy or a bone treatment.

This NOD2 marker is a replicated Crohn-disease susceptibility association, especially in some ancestry groups. It does not diagnose Crohn disease or explain symptoms by itself; GI symptoms, family history, blood/stool tests, and clinical evaluation matter more.

This NOD2 marker has been studied in intestinal immune response and Crohn-disease susceptibility. Any association is probabilistic and ancestry-dependent; it is not a diagnosis or a reason to begin a restrictive diet or medicine.

This NOD2 frameshift marker can be clinically important in Crohn-disease genetics, but a consumer-array result still requires validated testing and clinical interpretation. It does not diagnose IBD or determine treatment.

This ATG16L1 marker has been associated with Crohn-disease susceptibility and intestinal immune handling. It is a modest context signal, not a diagnosis; symptoms, inflammatory markers, stool testing, and GI review remain more useful.
This IL23R marker is part of research on IBD and Th17 immune signaling. Associations can vary by population and model; it does not diagnose IBD or predict whether an immune medicine will work.

translations.simpleImpact: FUT2 secretor-status and gut context marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This FUT2 marker can contribute to secretor-status and mucosal-glycan research, including some microbiome, infection, and B12 associations. It does not diagnose gut disease, determine a microbiome state, or prove B12 deficiency.

This ABCG8 marker has been studied in sterol transport and gallstone-related traits. It does not diagnose gallstones or determine a diet or surgery; symptoms and medical evaluation are more informative.

This sterol-transporter marker has been studied in cholesterol handling and gallstone-related traits. Effects are probabilistic and do not establish a gallbladder disorder or prescribe a low-fat diet.

This PNPLA3 marker has been associated with liver-fat or liver-injury traits in some populations. It does not diagnose fatty liver or steatohepatitis; metabolic health, alcohol exposure, liver tests, and imaging provide the actionable context.

This TM6SF2 marker has been studied in liver fat and blood-lipid traits. Associations can involve different phenotypes and do not diagnose liver disease or determine a medication; lipid and liver evaluation matter more.

translations.simpleImpact: MBOAT7 liver and lipid context marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This MBOAT7 marker is part of research on liver fat, inflammation, and lipid handling. It does not diagnose fatty liver or determine a detox product, supplement, or treatment; measured tests and clinical history lead.

This HSD17B13 splice-region marker has been studied in liver-fat and liver-injury outcomes. It does not establish protection or disease for one person; liver tests, imaging, metabolic factors, and clinician review remain important.

This FCGR2A marker has been studied in immune-complex handling and inflammatory disease associations. Effects vary and do not diagnose IBD or determine immune-treatment response; symptoms and clinical testing matter more.

This IL10-region marker has been studied in immune regulation and inflammatory-bowel traits. It is probabilistic research context, not an IBD diagnosis or a reason to start an immune medicine or restrictive diet.

This TTR marker is associated with an inherited transthyretin-amyloidosis variant, especially in some ancestry groups, but penetrance is age-dependent and incomplete. A consumer call is not a diagnosis; validated clinical testing and appropriate cardiac or neurologic evaluation are required.

translations.simpleImpact: Factor V Leiden clot-risk context marker
translations.simpleMeaning: This marker can represent Factor V Leiden, an inherited tendency toward venous blood clots. A consumer result needs clinical confirmation and personal or family history; it does not diagnose a current clot or by itself determine contraception, pregnancy, or anticoagulant treatment.

This marker can represent a prothrombin variant associated with venous-clot risk in some situations. Confirm it clinically and discuss personal or family history and exposures such as estrogen, surgery, or immobility; it does not diagnose a current clot or prescribe treatment.

This PCSK9 marker has been associated with lower LDL cholesterol in some studies. It is a probabilistic lipid context signal, not a guarantee of a healthy lipid profile or a reason to start or stop a cholesterol medicine; measured lipids and clinical history matter more.

This LDLR marker has been associated with small differences in LDL cholesterol. It is a common regulatory proxy, not the same as a pathogenic familial-hypercholesterolemia variant and not a substitute for a lipid panel or clinical assessment.

This liver-lipid locus has been associated with differences in LDL cholesterol and lipoprotein handling. Effects are probabilistic and small compared with the full clinical picture; it does not diagnose vascular disease or determine medication.

This ANGPTL4 marker has been studied in triglyceride and lipoprotein-lipase biology. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a lipid disorder or determine a diet, supplement, or medication; a measured lipid panel is more useful.

This TCF21 locus has been studied in coronary-artery disease and vascular-remodeling research. It is a small-effect association, not a diagnosis or a personal event prediction; blood pressure, lipids, smoking, diabetes, family history, and clinical care matter more.

translation_groups.simpleMeaning: This marker has been studied in research about how the body processes food, alcohol, fats, or other everyday exposures. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a condition or tell you what to consume; symptoms, measured tests, and clinical context matter more.

translation_groups.simpleImpact: Blood sugar and metabolism research context
translation_groups.simpleMeaning: This marker has been studied in research about blood sugar, insulin, appetite, body weight, or metabolism. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose diabetes or predict your weight; measured labs, health history, and clinical care matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about how the body handles nutrients such as folate, vitamins, minerals, or dietary fats. Any association is probabilistic and does not prove a deficiency or tell you to take a supplement; measured labs and diet context matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about serotonin, dopamine, stress response, memory, or other brain-related traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a mental-health condition or predict medication response; symptoms, treatment history, and clinician assessment matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about sleep timing, sleep duration, or sleep-related traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a sleep disorder or say how much sleep you need; sleep history and clinical evaluation matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about connective tissue, joints, tendons, or musculoskeletal traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a connective-tissue disorder, arthritis, or injury; symptoms and an appropriate clinical examination matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about thyroid regulation or immune traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose thyroid disease or an autoimmune condition; symptoms and measured thyroid or immune tests matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about blood pressure, cholesterol, blood vessels, or heart traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose heart disease or determine medication; measured lipids, blood pressure, history, and clinical care matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about allergy, airway, skin, or immune responses. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose an allergy, asthma, or mast-cell disorder; symptoms and appropriate clinical tests matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about digestion, the gut, or inflammation. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a digestive condition or prescribe a restrictive diet; symptoms, nutrition, and clinical evaluation matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about muscle performance, oxygen use, or recovery. Any association is probabilistic and does not predict performance or tell you how to train, eat, or supplement; your training history and health context matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about pigmentation, skin, hair, or related traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose a skin condition or determine your appearance; clinical examination and personal context matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about bone density, growth, or skeletal traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose osteoporosis or predict a fracture; age, nutrition, activity, medications, and measured bone health matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about kidney function, blood pressure, uric acid, minerals, or fluid balance. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose kidney disease or stones or justify changing salt or medication; measured tests and clinical history matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about lung function, airway inflammation, oxygen use, or smoking-related traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose asthma, COPD, or an inherited lung condition; symptoms and clinical testing matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about immune regulation and autoimmune conditions. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose an autoimmune disease or justify immune treatment; symptoms, laboratory testing, and clinician assessment matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about pain, migraine, temperature, taste, or other sensory traits. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose migraine or a pain disorder or dictate an analgesic; symptoms and clinical assessment matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about teeth, enamel, gums, or taste. Any association is probabilistic and does not diagnose dental disease; dental examination, hygiene, diet, and personal history matter more.

This marker has been studied in research about aging, inflammation, cell maintenance, or resilience. Any association is probabilistic and does not predict lifespan or current health; prevention, measured health factors, and clinical care matter more.
